status: Research revision; implementation prototype compiles but is not accuracy-qualified or visually verified.
design_authority: User wants clearly recognizable analog tuner, contemporary rather than old, warm, ultra-premium subtle materials and details, simple with few visible functions. Supersedes cold silver circular-disc concept.
method: Qualitative reading of public App Store featured reviews, a Reddit discussion, vendor documentation. Not a representative statistical sample; no complaint prevalence inferred. Historical complaints do not prove current defects.

competitors.name: TonalEnergy
competitors.positive: Comprehensive practice tool, drones, instrument modes, temperament support; 2025 review acknowledges learning curve but strongly praises value.
competitors.complaint: 2018 review: jumpy target display and difficult-to-find string mode. Historical only.
competitors.current_correction: Current iOS guide has Bar display, optional smiley, instrument-specific damping and string tuner from Tuner tab.

competitors.name: GuitarTuna
competitors.complaint: 2023 and 2024 reviews object to subscriptions for tunings, additional lessons/content, startup popups. December 2024 review reports microphone permission difficulty but later reports recovery.

competitors.name: Fender Tune
competitors.positive: Free tuning and helpful direction prompts; Reddit includes long-term satisfied users.
competitors.complaint: 2021/2024 reviews report automatic string identification instability and request manual target choice. These are unverified user experiences, not measured accuracy defects.

competitors.name: Tunable
competitors.positive: Readable pitch history, adjustable precision view, recording and practice tools; one-time purchase per official about page.
competitors.complaint: Insufficient primary-source negative evidence in reviewed sample to assert a recurring current problem. Strong direct competitor.

competitors.name: Pano Tuner
competitors.positive: Fast, simple, cross-instrument, paid edition no ads. Strong direct competitor to minimalist positioning.
competitors.complaint: Current release notes discuss Bluetooth and interruption recovery fixes; fixes are not evidence these bugs remain.

competitors.name: iStroboSoft
competitors.positive: Professional strobe, fine intonation use, large tablet display. Manufacturer claims 0.1-cent accuracy.
competitors.complaint: 2020 low-E jumping report; 2023 upside-down rotation complaint; June 1 review with year omitted reports octave jumps and audio-interface input failure. 2024 positive review explains strobe learning curve. Claims not independently reproduced.

competitors.name: Zen Tuner
competitors.positive: Free minimalist chromatic tuning with transposition; proves minimalism alone is not differentiation.
competitors.complaint: 2022 Mac USB audio-interface complaint; not evidence of iOS defect.

competitors.name: Cleartune
competitors.positive: Dedicated tuner with loyal long-term users and reference tones.
competitors.complaint: 2017 review objects to removed controls and changed workflow; historical regression lesson, not verified current bug.

positioning_hypothesis: A trustworthy everyday tuning instrument for musicians: fast entry, readable and honest pitch feedback, minimal interruption, coherent Clean series industrial design. No ads/subscription is a baseline, not unique.

precision_baseline.conditions: 1116 synthetic stationary windows, MIDI 28–89, offsets -30/0/+30 cents, 44.1/48 kHz, 8192 samples; three waveforms; no mic, room noise, dynamics, latency or competitor comparison.
precision_baseline.finding: Pure sine p95 5.03 cents and max 10.29; harmonic conditions include octave errors near 1200 cents. Current prototype cannot claim TonalEnergy parity.

proposed_quality_gates_not_achieved: Synthetic steady-tone p95 <=0.5 cent in declared supported range, with no octave errors in regression corpus.
Measure correct-note acquisition time, steady-state error, jitter and silence false positives on real instruments.
Run matched-device matched-signal comparison against TonalEnergy and Tunable with same A4, temperament, transposition, and documented damping.
Use independent known signal/reference to measure error, not only agreement between apps.
Cover low strings, weak fundamental, pluck attack/decay, vibrato, ambient noise, route changes, and 44.1/48 kHz.
product_revisions: Prioritize the pitch display and trustworthy lock over a large calibration block.
Instrument selection should not privilege guitar if claiming musician utility; include manual target lock.
Consider Tune and Sustain display modes only when backed by user needs; avoid a practice-suite expansion.
No claim of best accuracy, noise immunity or professional piano tuning.
A4-only tone and standard-guitar-only presets are prototype limitations, not final scope decisions.
